1	"""Batch label-update submission, validation and history.
2	
3	A batch file is a UTF-8 JSON object of the form::
4	
5	    {
6	      "batch": "non-empty batch number",
7	      "changes": [
8	        {"sha256": "<full SHA-256 digest>", "old": <string or null>,
9	         "new": <string or null>}
10	      ]
11	    }
12	
13	``null`` and the empty string both mean "unlabeled"; any other string is
14	taken literally (including Chinese text and a class named ``unlabeled``).
15	"""
16	
17	from __future__ import annotations
18	
19	from dataclasses import dataclass
20	from typing import Any, Callable, Iterator, Mapping
21	
22	BATCH_SCHEMA_VERSION = 1
23	
24	
25	@dataclass(frozen=True)
26	class BatchResolution:
27	    """One record's verdict, produced before anything is written.
28	
29	    ``current`` is the label read once during verification and ``changed``
30	    is whether ``new`` differs from it.  A resolution never references the
31	    manifest item or its revision, so the decision stays independent of
32	    the later workspace save.
33	    """
34	
35	    sha256: str
36	    old: str | None
37	    new: str | None
38	    current: str | None
39	    changed: bool
40	
41	
42	class BatchError(ValueError):
43	    """A batch submission or undo request is invalid."""
44	
45	
46	def normalize_label(label: Any) -> str | None:
47	    """Map the two unlabeled spellings to ``None``; keep strings literal.
48	
49	    Raises :class:`BatchError` for anything that is not a string or ``None``.
50	    """
51	    if label is None or label == "":
52	        return None
53	    if isinstance(label, str):
54	        return label
55	    raise BatchError(f"label must be a string or null, got {label!r}")
56	
57	
58	def render_label(label: str | None) -> str:
59	    """Human-readable rendering for messages."""
60	    return "unlabeled" if label is None else label
61	
62	
63	def parse_batch_file(data: Any) -> tuple[str, list[dict[str, Any]]]:
64	    """Validate a parsed batch payload; return ``(number, records)``.
65	
66	    Each record is ``{"sha256": str, "old": str | None, "new": str | None}``
67	    with labels normalized (``None`` for unlabeled).  Structural problems,
68	    an empty batch number and duplicate digests are all rejected here.
69	    """
70	    if not isinstance(data, dict):
71	        raise BatchError("batch file must contain a JSON object")
72	    number = data.get("batch")
73	    if not isinstance(number, str) or not number.strip():
74	        raise BatchError("batch number must be a non-empty string")
75	    changes = data.get("changes")
76	    if not isinstance(changes, list):
77	        raise BatchError("batch file must contain a 'changes' list")
78	
79	    records: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
80	    seen: set[str] = set()
81	    for index, change in enumerate(changes):
82	        location = f"change #{index + 1}"
83	        if not isinstance(change, dict):
84	            raise BatchError(
85	                f"{location}: must be an object with 'sha256', 'old' and 'new'"
86	            )
87	        if not all(key in change for key in ("sha256", "old", "new")):
88	            raise BatchError(
89	                f"{location}: must contain 'sha256', 'old' and 'new' keys"
90	            )
91	        digest = change["sha256"]
92	        if not isinstance(digest, str) or not digest:
93	            raise BatchError(f"{location}: 'sha256' must be a non-empty string")
94	        if digest in seen:
95	            raise BatchError(f"{location}: duplicate sample {digest}")
96	        seen.add(digest)
97	        old = normalize_label(change["old"])
98	        new = normalize_label(change["new"])
99	        records.append({"sha256": digest, "old": old, "new": new})
100	    return number, records
101	
102	
103	def content_key(records: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> frozenset[tuple[str, str | None, str | None]]:
104	    """Order- and spelling-insensitive identity of a batch's content.
105	
106	    Two submissions with the same number are considered the same batch
107	    when their record sets compare equal here: list order does not matter
108	    and ``null`` vs ``""`` does not matter.  Labels are normalized on both
109	    sides before comparing, so the equality also holds across the two
110	    places records come from — freshly parsed records (already normalized
111	    to ``None``) and history rows loaded from disk, which may have legally
112	    saved either unlabeled spelling.  Every other string is kept exactly,
113	    so a real class named ``unlabeled`` never matches an unlabeled record
114	    and case, surrounding whitespace, Chinese text and path separators
115	    stay significant.
116	    """
117	    return frozenset(
118	        (
119	            record["sha256"],
120	            normalize_label(record["old"]),
121	            normalize_label(record["new"]),
122	        )
123	        for record in records
124	    )
125	
126	
127	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
128	# Submission rules
129	#
130	# Each stage is a pure function of parsed records and the state passed to
131	# it; none of them mutate the manifest or the history.  The stages line up
132	# with the conditions that reject a submission, in their original order:
133	#
134	#   1. reject_unknown_samples  — records naming no registered sample
135	#   2. resolve_re_submission   — same-number history: replay or conflict
136	#   3. verify_records          — one current-label pass: old-label
137	#                                mismatches reject the whole batch; the
138	#                                surviving resolutions also decide which
139	#                                records actually change
140	#   4. apply_resolutions       — the only mutating stage (store layer)
141	#   5. build_history_entry / result_payload — result/history assembly
142	#
143	# "Current label" is read exactly once for the whole submission (stage 3),
144	# so verification and the change decision never process it twice.
145	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
146	
147	# A current-label lookup: full digest -> normalized current label (or
148	# ``None`` when the digest names no registered sample).
149	CurrentLabels = Callable[[str], str | None]
150	
151	
152	def reject_unknown_samples(
153	    records: list[dict[str, Any]], known: Callable[[str], bool]
154	) -> None:
155	    """Reject the batch if any record names a sample that is not registered.
156	
157	    The first unknown record is reported, in submission order.
158	    """
159	    for record in records:
160	        if not known(record["sha256"]):
161	            raise BatchError(f"sample not found: {record['sha256']}")
162	
163	
164	def resolve_re_submission(
165	    number: str,
166	    records: list[dict[str, Any]],
167	    existing: dict[str, Any] | None,
168	) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
169	    """Handle a batch number already present in history.
170	
171	    Equal content (per :func:`content_key`) replays the first submission's
172	    result without touching the manifest — even when samples have since
173	    changed — while different content conflicts.  Returns the replay
174	    result, or ``None`` when the number is free.
175	    """
176	    if existing is None:
177	        return None
178	    if content_key(existing["records"]) == content_key(records):
179	        return replay_result(existing)
180	    raise BatchError(
181	        f"batch number {number!r} is already used with different content"
182	    )
183	
184	
185	def verify_records(
186	    records: list[dict[str, Any]], current_label: CurrentLabels
187	) -> list[BatchResolution]:
188	    """Verify every expected old label and classify each record, in one pass.
189	
190	    Each record's current label is looked up once and used for both
191	    decisions: a current label differing from the expected old rejects the
192	    whole batch; otherwise the record is classified as changed only when
193	    the target label differs from that same current label.  No manifest
194	    item is modified here.
195	    """
196	    resolutions: list[BatchResolution] = []
197	    for record in records:
198	        current = current_label(record["sha256"])
199	        if current != record["old"]:
200	            raise BatchError(
201	                f"change for {record['sha256']}: expected old label "
202	                f"{render_label(record['old'])!r} but current label is "
203	                f"{render_label(current)!r}"
204	            )
205	        resolutions.append(
206	            BatchResolution(
207	                sha256=record["sha256"],
208	                old=record["old"],
209	                new=record["new"],
210	                current=current,
211	                changed=current != record["new"],
212	            )
213	        )
214	    return resolutions
215	
216	
217	def apply_resolutions(
218	    resolutions: list[BatchResolution],
219	    items: Mapping[str, dict[str, Any]],
220	) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
221	    """Mutate manifest items for the resolved records and build history rows.
222	
223	    This is the only stage that changes samples: records flagged
224	    ``changed`` receive their target label and a new revision; no-op
225	    records keep both.  Every row additionally records the revision after
226	    the batch, which later undos pin against.  The pre-change revision is
227	    read from each item here, once, rather than during verification.
228	    """
229	    applied: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
230	    for resolution in resolutions:
231	        item = items[resolution.sha256]
232	        revision = item_revision(item)
233	        if resolution.changed:
234	            item["label"] = resolution.new
235	            revision += 1
236	            item["rev"] = revision
237	        applied.append(
238	            {
239	                "sha256": resolution.sha256,
240	                "old": resolution.old,
241	                "new": resolution.new,
242	                "changed": resolution.changed,
243	                "rev": revision,
244	            }
245	        )
246	    return applied
247	
248	
249	def build_history_entry(
250	    number: str, applied_records: list[dict[str, Any]]
251	) -> dict[str, Any]:
252	    """Assemble the history row for a batch with at least one change."""
253	    return {
254	        "batch": number,
255	        "records": applied_records,
256	        "changed_count": sum(1 for record in applied_records if record["changed"]),
257	        "undone": False,
258	        "undone_at": None,
259	    }
260	
261	
262	def result_payload(
263	    number: str, status: str, applied_records: list[dict[str, Any]]
264	) -> dict[str, Any]:
265	    """Build the user-facing result, keeping the original count meanings.
266	
267	    ``changed`` counts records that actually changed a label,
268	    ``unchanged`` counts target-equals-current records and ``total``
269	    counts every submitted record.
270	    """
271	    changed = sum(1 for record in applied_records if record["changed"])
272	    return {
273	        "batch": number,
274	        "status": status,
275	        "changed": changed,
276	        "unchanged": len(applied_records) - changed,
277	        "total": len(applied_records),
278	    }
279	
280	
281	def no_changes_result(number: str, total: int) -> dict[str, Any]:
282	    """Result for a batch whose records all match their current labels."""
283	    return {
284	        "batch": number,
285	        "status": "no-changes",
286	        "changed": 0,
287	        "unchanged": total,
288	        "total": total,
289	    }
290	
291	
292	def replay_result(entry: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
293	    """Reconstruct the original result from a stored history entry."""
294	    return result_payload(entry["batch"], "already-applied", entry["records"])
295	
296	
297	def item_revision(item: dict[str, Any]) -> int:
298	    """Read a sample's label revision, treating malformed stored values as 0."""
299	    value = item.get("rev", 0)
300	    return value if isinstance(value, int) and not isinstance(value, bool) else 0
301	
302	
303	def describe_history_revision_problem(value: Any, *, present: bool) -> str | None:
304	    """Describe why a history record's ``rev`` is not a usable revision.
305	
306	    Every batch-history sample record must carry ``rev`` as a genuine
307	    non-negative integer: the revision pinned for later undos.  Booleans
308	    (``True == 1``), decimals (``1.0 == 1``), numeric strings (``"1"``),
309	    ``null`` and a missing field are all rejected rather than coerced, so
310	    they can never compare equal to a sample's current revision.  Returns
311	    ``None`` when the value is valid.
312	    """
313	    if not present:
314	        return "missing 'rev' field"
315	    if isinstance(value, bool):
316	        return f"'rev' must be a non-negative integer, got boolean {value!r}"
317	    if not isinstance(value, int):
318	        return f"'rev' must be a non-negative integer, got {value!r}"
319	    if value < 0:
320	        return f"'rev' must be a non-negative integer, got negative {value}"
321	    return None
322	
323	
324	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
325	# Undo-time integrity checks
326	#
327	# Every ``require_intact_history_*`` check scans the same record list of
328	# the same target batch entry, so the shared mechanics live in two
329	# helpers: ``_iter_history_records`` reads the list once, rejects a
330	# missing list or a non-object row and yields ``(position, record)``
331	# pairs; ``_corruption_prefix`` and ``_record_ref`` assemble the common
332	# "Batch history is corrupted: batch ..." message parts.  The checks
333	# themselves stay separate passes and keep their original order —
334	# duplicate digests, then revisions, then labels, then changed flags —
335	# each reporting its first problem in record order.
336	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
337	
338	
339	def _corruption_prefix(entry: Mapping[str, Any]) -> str:
340	    """Shared prefix of every batch-history corruption message."""
341	    return f"Batch history is corrupted: batch {entry.get('batch')!r}"
342	
343	
344	def _record_ref(record: Mapping[str, Any], position: int | None = None) -> str:
345	    """Locate a history record by sample digest and optional 1-based position."""
346	    ref = f"sample {record.get('sha256')}"
347	    if position is not None:
348	        ref += f", record #{position}"
349	    return ref
350	
351	
352	def _iter_history_records(
353	    entry: Mapping[str, Any],
354	) -> Iterator[tuple[int, Mapping[str, Any]]]:
355	    """Yield ``(position, record)`` for each row of a batch history entry.
356	
357	    This is the shared front half of every integrity check: the entry
358	    must carry a record list and every row must be an object.  Positions
359	    are 1-based, matching the record numbers used in error messages.
360	    """
361	    prefix = _corruption_prefix(entry)
362	    records = entry.get("records")
363	    if not isinstance(records, list):
364	        # validate_history() already rules this out; defend direct callers.
365	        raise BatchError(f"{prefix}: missing records")
366	    for position, record in enumerate(records, start=1):
367	        if not isinstance(record, dict):
368	            raise BatchError(f"{prefix}: malformed record")
369	        yield position, record
370	
371	
372	def require_intact_history_records(entry: Mapping[str, Any]) -> None:
373	    """Reject a batch entry whose records are not one row per sample.
374	
375	    Undo pins every stored record to a sample content digest, so a digest
376	    may occur at most once in the target batch: a duplicated row — even a
377	    byte-for-byte copy, or a copy of a record that never changed a label —
378	    would otherwise restore the same sample more than once, bump its label
379	    revision repeatedly and inflate the restored count.  Duplicates are
380	    therefore batch-history corruption, never records to merge or
381	    de-duplicate.  The decision is independent of the labels, the
382	    before/after labels and the record's ``changed`` flag: the content
383	    digest alone decides.
384	
385	    The whole record list is scanned, so rows preceding the repeat are
386	    checked too and a restorable row at the front can never mask a later
387	    duplicate.  On a repeat the error names the batch number, the sample's
388	    full digest and both 1-based record positions; nothing is repaired.
389	
390	    Callers must run this before any success-shaped short-circuit (such as
391	    an already-undone batch), so corruption can never be masked by a
392	    repeated-undo success.
393	    """
394	    seen: dict[str, int] = {}
395	    for position, record in _iter_history_records(entry):
396	        digest = record.get("sha256")
397	        if digest in seen:
398	            raise BatchError(
399	                f"{_corruption_prefix(entry)}, sample {digest} "
400	                f"appears more than once, at record #{seen[digest]} and "
401	                f"record #{position}"
402	            )
403	        seen[digest] = position
404	
405	
406	def require_intact_history_revisions(entry: Mapping[str, Any]) -> None:
407	    """Reject a batch entry whose records lack a sound pinned ``rev``.
408	
409	    Every record — changed or not — must carry ``rev`` as a genuine
410	    non-negative integer, since undo pins each changed sample to the

415	    full digest and the exact ``rev`` problem, and nothing is repaired.

418	    an already-undone batch), so corruption can never be masked by a

477	        problem = describe_missing_history_labels(record)
478	        if problem is not None:

480	                f"{_corruption_prefix(entry)}, "
481	                f"{_record_ref(record, position)}: {problem}"
482	            )

485	def history_labels_equal(old: Any, new: Any) -> bool:
486	    """Whether two stored history labels describe the same category.
487	
488	    The decision uses the labels saved in the history record itself, never
489	    a sample's current label: ``null`` and the empty string both mean
490	    unlabeled and are therefore equal, while every other value is compared
491	    as the exact original string — case, surrounding whitespace, Chinese
492	    text and path separators all keep their meaning, and a real class
493	    literally named ``unlabeled`` never equals unlabeled.
494	    """
495	    return normalize_label(old) == normalize_label(new)
496	
497	
498	def describe_history_change_problem(record: Mapping[str, Any]) -> str | None:
499	    """Describe why a history record's ``changed`` flag contradicts old/new.
500	
501	    The flag must agree with the before/after labels saved on that same
502	    record: differing labels require ``changed: true`` and equal labels
503	    require ``changed: false``.  Returns ``None`` when the flag is
504	    consistent.  The stored labels are validated upstream as strings or
505	    ``None`` and the flag as a boolean, so no type guessing happens here.
506	    """
507	    actually_changed = not history_labels_equal(record["old"], record["new"])
508	    old_label = normalize_label(record["old"])
509	    new_label = normalize_label(record["new"])
510	    if actually_changed and not record["changed"]:
511	        return (
512	            f"'changed' is false but the before/after labels differ: "
513	            f"{render_label(old_label)!r} -> {render_label(new_label)!r}"

517	            f"'changed' is true but the before/after labels are identical: "
518	            f"{render_label(old_label)!r}"
519	        )

540	    the batch number, the sample's full SHA-256 digest and the record's
541	    1-based position inside the target batch, together with the exact

543

556	                f"{_record_ref(record, position)}: {problem}"

561	    return {"schema_version": BATCH_SCHEMA_VERSION, "batches": []}

565	    """Validate a loaded batch history payload; return it unchanged."""

"""Batch label-update submission, validation and history.

A batch file is a UTF-8 JSON object of the form::

    {
      "batch": "non-empty batch number",
      "changes": [
        {"sha256": "<full SHA-256 digest>", "old": <string or null>,
         "new": <string or null>}
      ]
    }

``null`` and the empty string both mean "unlabeled"; any other string is
taken literally (including Chinese text and a class named ``unlabeled``).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Any, Callable, Iterator, Mapping

BATCH_SCHEMA_VERSION = 1


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class BatchResolution:
    """One record's verdict, produced before anything is written.

    ``current`` is the label read once during verification and ``changed``
    is whether ``new`` differs from it.  A resolution never references the
    manifest item or its revision, so the decision stays independent of
    the later workspace save.
    """

    sha256: str
    old: str | None
    new: str | None
    current: str | None
    changed: bool


class BatchError(ValueError):
    """A batch submission or undo request is invalid."""


def normalize_label(label: Any) -> str | None:
    """Map the two unlabeled spellings to ``None``; keep strings literal.

    Raises :class:`BatchError` for anything that is not a string or ``None``.
    """
    if label is None or label == "":
        return None
    if isinstance(label, str):
        return label
    raise BatchError(f"label must be a string or null, got {label!r}")


def render_label(label: str | None) -> str:
    """Human-readable rendering for messages."""
    return "unlabeled" if label is None else label


def parse_batch_file(data: Any) -> tuple[str, list[dict[str, Any]]]:
    """Validate a parsed batch payload; return ``(number, records)``.

    Each record is ``{"sha256": str, "old": str | None, "new": str | None}``
    with labels normalized (``None`` for unlabeled).  Structural problems,
    an empty batch number and duplicate digests are all rejected here.
    """
    if not isinstance(data, dict):
        raise BatchError("batch file must contain a JSON object")
    number = data.get("batch")
    if not isinstance(number, str) or not number.strip():
        raise BatchError("batch number must be a non-empty string")
    changes = data.get("changes")
    if not isinstance(changes, list):
        raise BatchError("batch file must contain a 'changes' list")

    records: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    seen: set[str] = set()
    for index, change in enumerate(changes):
        location = f"change #{index + 1}"
        if not isinstance(change, dict):
            raise BatchError(
                f"{location}: must be an object with 'sha256', 'old' and 'new'"
            )
        if not all(key in change for key in ("sha256", "old", "new")):
            raise BatchError(
                f"{location}: must contain 'sha256', 'old' and 'new' keys"
            )
        digest = change["sha256"]
        if not isinstance(digest, str) or not digest:
            raise BatchError(f"{location}: 'sha256' must be a non-empty string")
        if digest in seen:
            raise BatchError(f"{location}: duplicate sample {digest}")
        seen.add(digest)
        old = normalize_label(change["old"])
        new = normalize_label(change["new"])
        records.append({"sha256": digest, "old": old, "new": new})
    return number, records


def content_key(records: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> frozenset[tuple[str, str | None, str | None]]:
    """Order- and spelling-insensitive identity of a batch's content.

    Two submissions with the same number are considered the same batch
    when their record sets compare equal here: list order does not matter
    and ``null`` vs ``""`` does not matter.  Labels are normalized on both
    sides before comparing, so the equality also holds across the two
    places records come from — freshly parsed records (already normalized
    to ``None``) and history rows loaded from disk, which may have legally
    saved either unlabeled spelling.  Every other string is kept exactly,
    so a real class named ``unlabeled`` never matches an unlabeled record
    and case, surrounding whitespace, Chinese text and path separators
    stay significant.
    """
    return frozenset(
        (
            record["sha256"],
            normalize_label(record["old"]),
            normalize_label(record["new"]),
        )
        for record in records
    )


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Submission rules
#
# Each stage is a pure function of parsed records and the state passed to
# it; none of them mutate the manifest or the history.  The stages line up
# with the conditions that reject a submission, in their original order:
#
#   1. reject_unknown_samples  — records naming no registered sample
#   2. resolve_re_submission   — same-number history: replay or conflict
#   3. verify_records          — one current-label pass: old-label
#                                mismatches reject the whole batch; the
#                                surviving resolutions also decide which
#                                records actually change
#   4. apply_resolutions       — the only mutating stage (store layer)
#   5. build_history_entry / result_payload — result/history assembly
#
# "Current label" is read exactly once for the whole submission (stage 3),
# so verification and the change decision never process it twice.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# A current-label lookup: full digest -> normalized current label (or
# ``None`` when the digest names no registered sample).
CurrentLabels = Callable[[str], str | None]


def reject_unknown_samples(
    records: list[dict[str, Any]], known: Callable[[str], bool]
) -> None:
    """Reject the batch if any record names a sample that is not registered.

    The first unknown record is reported, in submission order.
    """
    for record in records:
        if not known(record["sha256"]):
            raise BatchError(f"sample not found: {record['sha256']}")


def resolve_re_submission(
    number: str,
    records: list[dict[str, Any]],
    existing: dict[str, Any] | None,
) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
    """Handle a batch number already present in history.

    Equal content (per :func:`content_key`) replays the first submission's
    result without touching the manifest — even when samples have since
    changed — while different content conflicts.  Returns the replay
    result, or ``None`` when the number is free.
    """
    if existing is None:
        return None
    if content_key(existing["records"]) == content_key(records):
        return replay_result(existing)
    raise BatchError(
        f"batch number {number!r} is already used with different content"
    )


def verify_records(
    records: list[dict[str, Any]], current_label: CurrentLabels
) -> list[BatchResolution]:
    """Verify every expected old label and classify each record, in one pass.

    Each record's current label is looked up once and used for both
    decisions: a current label differing from the expected old rejects the
    whole batch; otherwise the record is classified as changed only when
    the target label differs from that same current label.  No manifest
    item is modified here.
    """
    resolutions: list[BatchResolution] = []
    for record in records:
        current = current_label(record["sha256"])
        if current != record["old"]:
            raise BatchError(
                f"change for {record['sha256']}: expected old label "
                f"{render_label(record['old'])!r} but current label is "
                f"{render_label(current)!r}"
            )
        resolutions.append(
            BatchResolution(
                sha256=record["sha256"],
                old=record["old"],
                new=record["new"],
                current=current,
                changed=current != record["new"],
            )
        )
    return resolutions


def apply_resolutions(
    resolutions: list[BatchResolution],
    items: Mapping[str, dict[str, Any]],
) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    """Mutate manifest items for the resolved records and build history rows.

    This is the only stage that changes samples: records flagged
    ``changed`` receive their target label and a new revision; no-op
    records keep both.  Every row additionally records the revision after
    the batch, which later undos pin against.  The pre-change revision is
    read from each item here, once, rather than during verification.
    """
    applied: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    for resolution in resolutions:
        item = items[resolution.sha256]
        revision = item_revision(item)
        if resolution.changed:
            item["label"] = resolution.new
            revision += 1
            item["rev"] = revision
        applied.append(
            {
                "sha256": resolution.sha256,
                "old": resolution.old,
                "new": resolution.new,
                "changed": resolution.changed,
                "rev": revision,
            }
        )
    return applied


def build_history_entry(
    number: str, applied_records: list[dict[str, Any]]
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Assemble the history row for a batch with at least one change."""
    return {
        "batch": number,
        "records": applied_records,
        "changed_count": sum(1 for record in applied_records if record["changed"]),
        "undone": False,
        "undone_at": None,
    }


def result_payload(
    number: str, status: str, applied_records: list[dict[str, Any]]
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Build the user-facing result, keeping the original count meanings.

    ``changed`` counts records that actually changed a label,
    ``unchanged`` counts target-equals-current records and ``total``
    counts every submitted record.
    """
    changed = sum(1 for record in applied_records if record["changed"])
    return {
        "batch": number,
        "status": status,
        "changed": changed,
        "unchanged": len(applied_records) - changed,
        "total": len(applied_records),
    }


def no_changes_result(number: str, total: int) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Result for a batch whose records all match their current labels."""
    return {
        "batch": number,
        "status": "no-changes",
        "changed": 0,
        "unchanged": total,
        "total": total,
    }


def replay_result(entry: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Reconstruct the original result from a stored history entry."""
    return result_payload(entry["batch"], "already-applied", entry["records"])


def item_revision(item: dict[str, Any]) -> int:
    """Read a sample's label revision, treating malformed stored values as 0."""
    value = item.get("rev", 0)
    return value if isinstance(value, int) and not isinstance(value, bool) else 0


def describe_history_revision_problem(value: Any, *, present: bool) -> str | None:
    """Describe why a history record's ``rev`` is not a usable revision.

    Every batch-history sample record must carry ``rev`` as a genuine
    non-negative integer: the revision pinned for later undos.  Booleans
    (``True == 1``), decimals (``1.0 == 1``), numeric strings (``"1"``),
    ``null`` and a missing field are all rejected rather than coerced, so
    they can never compare equal to a sample's current revision.  Returns
    ``None`` when the value is valid.
    """
    if not present:
        return "missing 'rev' field"
    if isinstance(value, bool):
        return f"'rev' must be a non-negative integer, got boolean {value!r}"
    if not isinstance(value, int):
        return f"'rev' must be a non-negative integer, got {value!r}"
    if value < 0:
        return f"'rev' must be a non-negative integer, got negative {value}"
    return None


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Undo-time integrity checks
#
# Every ``require_intact_history_*`` check scans the same record list of
# the same target batch entry, so the shared mechanics live in two
# helpers: ``_iter_history_records`` reads the list once, rejects a
# missing list or a non-object row and yields ``(position, record)``
# pairs; ``_corruption_prefix`` and ``_record_ref`` assemble the common
# "Batch history is corrupted: batch ..." message parts.  The checks
# themselves stay separate passes and keep their original order —
# duplicate digests, then revisions, then labels, then changed flags —
# each reporting its first problem in record order.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def _corruption_prefix(entry: Mapping[str, Any]) -> str:
    """Shared prefix of every batch-history corruption message."""
    return f"Batch history is corrupted: batch {entry.get('batch')!r}"


def _record_ref(record: Mapping[str, Any], position: int | None = None) -> str:
    """Locate a history record by sample digest and optional 1-based position."""
    ref = f"sample {record.get('sha256')}"
    if position is not None:
        ref += f", record #{position}"
    return ref


def _iter_history_records(
    entry: Mapping[str, Any],
) -> Iterator[tuple[int, Mapping[str, Any]]]:
    """Yield ``(position, record)`` for each row of a batch history entry.

    This is the shared front half of every integrity check: the entry
    must carry a record list and every row must be an object.  Positions
    are 1-based, matching the record numbers used in error messages.
    """
    prefix = _corruption_prefix(entry)
    records = entry.get("records")
    if not isinstance(records, list):
        # validate_history() already rules this out; defend direct callers.
        raise BatchError(f"{prefix}: missing records")
    for position, record in enumerate(records, start=1):
        if not isinstance(record, dict):
            raise BatchError(f"{prefix}: malformed record")
        yield position, record


def require_intact_history_records(entry: Mapping[str, Any]) -> None:
    """Reject a batch entry whose records are not one row per sample.

    Undo pins every stored record to a sample content digest, so a digest
    may occur at most once in the target batch: a duplicated row — even a
    byte-for-byte copy, or a copy of a record that never changed a label —
    would otherwise restore the same sample more than once, bump its label
    revision repeatedly and inflate the restored count.  Duplicates are
    therefore batch-history corruption, never records to merge or
    de-duplicate.  The decision is independent of the labels, the
    before/after labels and the record's ``changed`` flag: the content
    digest alone decides.

    The whole record list is scanned, so rows preceding the repeat are
    checked too and a restorable row at the front can never mask a later
    duplicate.  On a repeat the error names the batch number, the sample's
    full digest and both 1-based record positions; nothing is repaired.

    Callers must run this before any success-shaped short-circuit (such as
    an already-undone batch), so corruption can never be masked by a
    repeated-undo success.
    """
    seen: dict[str, int] = {}
    for position, record in _iter_history_records(entry):
        digest = record.get("sha256")
        if digest in seen:
            raise BatchError(
                f"{_corruption_prefix(entry)}, sample {digest} "
                f"appears more than once, at record #{seen[digest]} and "
                f"record #{position}"
            )
        seen[digest] = position


def require_intact_history_revisions(entry: Mapping[str, Any]) -> None:
    """Reject a batch entry whose records lack a sound pinned ``rev``.

    Every record — changed or not — must carry ``rev`` as a genuine
    non-negative integer, since undo pins each changed sample to the
    revision it had at the end of the batch.  This is integrity damage,
    unlike the *manifest's* optional revision (see
    :func:`item_revision`, which keeps the legacy missing-means-zero
    behaviour): a bad row is reported with the batch number, the sample's
    full digest and the exact ``rev`` problem, and nothing is repaired.

    Callers must run this before any success-shaped short-circuit (such as
    an already-undone batch), so corruption can never be masked by a
    repeated-undo success.
    """
    for _position, record in _iter_history_records(entry):
        problem = describe_history_revision_problem(
            record.get("rev"), present="rev" in record
        )
        if problem is not None:
            raise BatchError(
                f"{_corruption_prefix(entry)}, "
                f"{_record_ref(record)}: {problem}"
            )


def describe_missing_history_labels(record: Mapping[str, Any]) -> str | None:
    """Describe which of a history record's before/after labels are absent.

    Every batch-history sample record must spell out both ``old`` (the
    label before the batch) and ``new`` (the label after it).  Only key
    presence is judged here: an explicitly saved ``null`` or empty string
    is a recorded unlabeled label, never a missing field.  Returns
    ``None`` when both keys are present.
    """
    missing = [key for key in ("old", "new") if key not in record]
    if not missing:
        return None
    if len(missing) == 2:
        return "missing 'old' and 'new' labels"
    return f"missing {missing[0]!r} label"


def require_intact_history_labels(entry: Mapping[str, Any]) -> None:
    """Reject a batch entry whose records lack a saved before/after label.

    Undo restores and counts samples purely from what the target batch's
    history rows say: a changed row is restored from ``new`` back to
    ``old``, an unchanged row is left alone.  That is only meaningful
    when every row explicitly carries both labels, so a row missing
    ``old``, ``new`` or both is batch-history corruption — never an
    unlabeled-to-unlabeled no-op to skip, and never something to guess
    from the sample's current label.  The error names the batch number,
    the sample's full SHA-256 digest, the record's 1-based position
    inside the target batch and which of ``old``/``new`` (or both) is
    absent; nothing is repaired, rewritten or restored.

    An explicitly saved ``null`` or empty string stays legal: both mean
    unlabeled, as does a literal class named ``unlabeled`` stay an
    ordinary label.  Only a missing key is damage.

    The whole record list is scanned in order — unchanged rows and rows
    behind restorable ones included — so a complete row at the front can
    never mask a damaged one further back, and no sample is restored
    before the damage is found.

    Callers must run this before any success-shaped short-circuit (such
    as an already-undone batch), so corruption can never be masked by a
    repeated-undo success.
    """
    for position, record in _iter_history_records(entry):
        problem = describe_missing_history_labels(record)
        if problem is not None:
            raise BatchError(
                f"{_corruption_prefix(entry)}, "
                f"{_record_ref(record, position)}: {problem}"
            )


def history_labels_equal(old: Any, new: Any) -> bool:
    """Whether two stored history labels describe the same category.

    The decision uses the labels saved in the history record itself, never
    a sample's current label: ``null`` and the empty string both mean
    unlabeled and are therefore equal, while every other value is compared
    as the exact original string — case, surrounding whitespace, Chinese
    text and path separators all keep their meaning, and a real class
    literally named ``unlabeled`` never equals unlabeled.
    """
    return normalize_label(old) == normalize_label(new)


def describe_history_change_problem(record: Mapping[str, Any]) -> str | None:
    """Describe why a history record's ``changed`` flag contradicts old/new.

    The flag must agree with the before/after labels saved on that same
    record: differing labels require ``changed: true`` and equal labels
    require ``changed: false``.  Returns ``None`` when the flag is
    consistent.  The stored labels are validated upstream as strings or
    ``None`` and the flag as a boolean, so no type guessing happens here.
    """
    actually_changed = not history_labels_equal(record["old"], record["new"])
    old_label = normalize_label(record["old"])
    new_label = normalize_label(record["new"])
    if actually_changed and not record["changed"]:
        return (
            f"'changed' is false but the before/after labels differ: "
            f"{render_label(old_label)!r} -> {render_label(new_label)!r}"
        )
    if not actually_changed and record["changed"]:
        return (
            f"'changed' is true but the before/after labels are identical: "
            f"{render_label(old_label)!r}"
        )
    return None


def require_intact_history_changes(entry: Mapping[str, Any]) -> None:
    """Reject a batch entry whose ``changed`` flags belie old/new labels.

    Undo restores a sample based on what the history row says the batch
    did: a row marked changed is restored from ``new`` back to ``old`` and
    counted, while a row marked unchanged is never restored.  So the flag
    must match the before/after labels saved on that row — judging from the
    record's own stored labels rather than any sample's current label:

    * differing old/new (``null`` and ``""`` being the same unlabeled
      spelling) require ``changed: true``;
    * identical old/new require ``changed: false``.

    A row that claims a change with identical labels would make undo count
    and restore a sample the batch never touched; a row that hides a real
    change would leave the sample at its post-batch label while the batch
    is recorded undone.  Both are batch-history corruption: the error names
    the batch number, the sample's full SHA-256 digest and the record's
    1-based position inside the target batch, together with the exact
    contradiction, and nothing is repaired.

    The whole record list is scanned in order, so a restorable row at the
    front can never mask a contradiction further back.

    Callers must run this before any success-shaped short-circuit (such as
    an already-undone batch), so corruption can never be masked by a
    repeated-undo success.
    """
    for position, record in _iter_history_records(entry):
        problem = describe_history_change_problem(record)
        if problem is not None:
            raise BatchError(
                f"{_corruption_prefix(entry)}, "
                f"{_record_ref(record, position)}: {problem}"
            )


def empty_history() -> dict[str, Any]:
    return {"schema_version": BATCH_SCHEMA_VERSION, "batches": []}


def validate_history(data: Any) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Validate a loaded batch history payload; return it unchanged."""
    if not isinstance(data, dict) or data.get("schema_version") != BATCH_SCHEMA_VERSION:
        raise BatchError("Unsupported batch history")
    batches = data.get("batches")
    if not isinstance(batches, list):
        raise BatchError("Malformed batch history")
    for entry in batches:
        if not isinstance(entry, dict):
            raise BatchError("Malformed batch history entry")
        if not isinstance(entry.get("batch"), str) or not entry["batch"].strip():
            raise BatchError("Malformed batch history entry: missing batch number")
        if not isinstance(entry.get("records"), list):
            raise BatchError("Malformed batch history entry: missing records")
        changed_count = entry.get("changed_count")
        if not isinstance(changed_count, int) or isinstance(changed_count, bool):
            raise BatchError("Malformed batch history entry: bad changed_count")
        if not isinstance(entry.get("undone"), bool):
            raise BatchError("Malformed batch history entry: bad undone flag")
        for record in entry["records"]:
            if not isinstance(record, dict):
                raise BatchError("Malformed batch history record")
            if not isinstance(record.get("sha256"), str):
                raise BatchError("Malformed batch history record: bad digest")
            for key in ("old", "new"):
                value = record.get(key)
                if value is not None and not isinstance(value, str):
                    raise BatchError("Malformed batch history record: bad label")
            if not isinstance(record.get("changed"), bool):
                raise BatchError("Malformed batch history record: bad changed flag")
    return data

465	                elif is_dir:
466	                    subdirectory = directory / name
467	                    # Open the confirmed subdirectory through the pinned
468	                    # parent with O_NOFOLLOW and scan the descriptor
469	                    # itself: a symlink swapped onto the path by now fails
470	                    # the whole import here, and the link target is never
471	                    # scanned.
472	                    try:
473	                        child_fd = self._open_real_directory(
474	                            name, parent_fd, subdirectory
475	                        )
476	                    except OSError as error:
477	                        raise ValueError(
478	                            f"cannot scan directory {subdirectory}: {error}"
479	                        ) from error
480	                    try:
481	                        child_entries = classify(subdirectory, child_fd)
482	                        confirmed_dirs.append(subdirectory)
483	                        walk(
484	                            subdirectory,
485	                            rel_prefix + name + "/",
486	                            child_fd,
487	                            child_entries,
488	                        )
489	                    finally:
490	                        os.close(child_fd)

492	        try:
493	            root_fd = self._open_real_directory(str(root), None, root)
494	        except OSError as error:
495	            raise ValueError(f"cannot scan directory {root}: {error}") from error
496	        try:
497	            walk(root, "", root_fd, classify(root, root))
498	        finally:
499	            os.close(root_fd)
500	        # Unicode code point order on the slash-separated relative path.
501	        rel_paths.sort()

504	    @staticmethod
505	    def _open_real_directory(name: str, dir_fd: int | None, path: Path) -> int:
506	        """Open a confirmed directory, refusing a symlink swapped onto it.
507	
508	        The open uses ``O_DIRECTORY | O_NOFOLLOW`` — relative to the
509	        pinned parent descriptor when ``dir_fd`` is given — so a symbolic
510	        link (or any non-directory) that replaced the confirmed directory
511	        is never descended through.  A symlink swap raises the import's
512	        "directory changed" error naming the replaced path; any other
513	        open failure propagates as the underlying :class:`OSError`.
514	        """
515	        try:
516	            return os.open(name, _DIRECTORY_OPEN_FLAGS, dir_fd=dir_fd)
517	        except OSError as error:
518	            # Linux reports a symlink opened with O_NOFOLLOW|O_DIRECTORY
519	            # as ENOTDIR rather than ELOOP, so confirm via lstat() either
520	            # way.
521	            if error.errno in (errno.ELOOP, errno.ENOTDIR):
522	                try:
523	                    current = os.lstat(path)
524	                except OSError:
525	                    current = None
526	                if current is not None and stat.S_ISLNK(current.st_mode):
527	                    raise ValueError(
528	                        f"directory changed during import: {path} "
529	                        "is now a symbolic link"
530	                    ) from error
531	            raise

533	    @staticmethod
534	    def _raise_if_now_symlink(directory: Path) -> None:
535	        """Fail if a previously confirmed real directory is now a symlink.
536	
537	        A path that vanished is left to the candidate reads (or ignored
538	        when the directory held no candidates); only the symlink swap is
539	        rejected here, because following the link would import the target's
540	        images against the no-symlinked-directories rule.
541	        """
542	        try:
543	            current = os.lstat(directory)
544	        except OSError:
545	            return
546	        if stat.S_ISLNK(current.st_mode):
547	            raise ValueError(
548	                f"directory changed during import: {directory} "
549	                "is now a symbolic link"
550	            )

552	    def _read_candidate(
553	        self, path: Path, rel_path: str
554	    ) -> tuple[str, Path, str, int]:
555	        """Read one candidate in full, verifying identity/size/mtime around it.
556	
557	        Returns ``(rel_path, absolute_path, digest, size)``.  A mismatch or
558	        read failure raises before the batch is committed.
559	
560	        Every ancestor directory of the candidate is re-opened from the
561	        source root with ``O_DIRECTORY | O_NOFOLLOW``, each relative to its
562	        pinned parent, and the candidate itself is opened relative to its
563	        pinned parent directory: a subdirectory replaced by a symbolic
564	        link since the scan fails the whole import here, and the link
565	        target's images are never opened — no matter when the swap lands.
566	        """
567	        parts = Path(rel_path).parts
568	        root = path
569	        for _ in parts:
570	            root = root.parent
571	        try:
572	            fd = self._open_real_directory(str(root), None, root)
573	        except OSError as error:
574	            raise ValueError(f"cannot read {rel_path}: {error}") from error
575	        try:
576	            ancestor = root
577	            for part in parts[:-1]:
578	                ancestor = ancestor / part
579	                try:
580	                    next_fd = self._open_real_directory(part, fd, ancestor)
581	                except OSError as error:
582	                    raise ValueError(
583	                        f"cannot read {rel_path}: {error}"
584	                    ) from error
585	                os.close(fd)
586	                fd = next_fd
587	            digest, size = self._read_stable(
588	                path, rel_path, dir_fd=fd, name=parts[-1]
589	            )
590	        finally:
591	            os.close(fd)
592	        return rel_path, path, digest, size
593	
594	    @staticmethod
595	    def _read_stable(
596	        path: Path,
597	        display: str,
598	        *,
599	        dir_fd: int | None = None,
600	        name: str | None = None,
601	    ) -> tuple[str, int]:
602	        """Read one file in full and return ``(digest, size)`` for it.
603	
604	        The digest and size are guaranteed to describe the same stable
605	        regular file: the path is lstat()ed without following symlinks
606	        and opened with ``O_NOFOLLOW``, the opened descriptor is
607	        fstat()ed to prove it is the inode that was confirmed, and the
608	        path is lstat()ed again after the read, requiring the same
609	        object with the same size and modification time.  Any identity,
610	        size or modification-time change — in-place rewrites, appends,
611	        truncation, delete-and-recreate, or replacing the path with
612	        another file, even one with identical content, size and mtime —
613	        fails with the path and reason, as do a vanishing path, a
614	        non-regular file and any open or read error.
615	
616	        The confirm/open/prove rule itself lives in :mod:`confirmed`
617	        and is shared with the source-directory export; only the
618	        post-read stability requirement and the import wording are
619	        specific to this entry point.
620	
621	        When ``dir_fd`` and ``name`` are given (whole-directory import),
622	        the pre-open inspection and the post-read re-inspection stay on
623	        the path, but the open itself is ``name`` relative to the pinned
624	        parent directory descriptor: an ancestor directory replaced by a
625	        symbolic link can never redirect the open into the link target.
626	        """
627	        try:
628	            if dir_fd is None:
629	                opened_file = confirmed.confirm_and_open_regular(path)
630	            else:
631	                confirmed_status = confirmed.inspect_regular(path)
632	                descriptor = confirmed.open_without_follow(name, dir_fd=dir_fd)
633	                opened_file = confirmed.ConfirmedOpen(
634	                    descriptor,
635	                    confirmed_status,
636	                    confirmed.prove_opened_regular(descriptor, confirmed_status),
637	                )
638	        except confirmed.ConfirmationError as failure:
639	            raise _import_confirmation_error(failure, display) from failure
640	        try:
641	            digest = confirmed.hash_descriptor(opened_file.descriptor)
642	        except OSError as error:
643	            raise ValueError(f"cannot read {display}: {error}") from error
644	        # Import, unlike export, also requires the path itself to still
645	        # name the same unchanged file after the read: an in-place
646	        # rewrite, append, truncation or replacement that landed while
647	        # the bytes were streamed must not register a digest/size pair
648	        # that never coexisted.
649	        try:
650	            after = os.lstat(path)
651	        except OSError as error:
652	            raise ValueError(f"cannot read {display}: {error}") from error
653	        if not confirmed.same_identity_size_mtime(opened_file.confirmed, after):
654	            raise ValueError(
655	                f"file changed during import: {display} "
656	                "(identity, size or modification time changed)"
657	            )
658	        return digest, opened_file.confirmed.st_size

671	    def find_by_label(self, label: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
672	        """List samples currently registered under one exact category label.
673	
674	        Matching is exact on the current manifest label: case, surrounding
675	        whitespace and path separators are all kept literally, so ``"cat"``
676	        never matches ``"Cat"`` or ``"cat "``.  The empty string queries
677	        unlabeled samples — records whose stored label is ``None`` or ``""``
678	        — and every matching record's label is reported uniformly as
679	        ``None``.  A genuine class literally named ``"unlabeled"`` is
680	        queried with that text and never mixed with unlabeled samples,
681	        unlike :meth:`summary` which merges them under one display key.
682	
683	        Each record provides the full SHA-256 digest, the source path saved
684	        at first registration, the byte size and the current label;
685	        records are sorted ascending by full digest and ``count`` always
686	        equals the list length.  The query reads the registered records
687	        only — it never opens a source file, and saved split plans' old
688	        labels are neither matched nor rewritten — so a moved, deleted or
689	        unreadable source is still found, and a batch update or undo
690	        committed before the call is immediately reflected.
691	        """
692	        if not isinstance(label, str):
693	            raise BatchError("query label must be a string")
694	        want_unlabeled = label == ""
695	        samples: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
696	        self.initialize()
697	        with self._locked():
698	            items = self._read()["items"]
699	        for item in items:
700	            stored = item.get("label")
701	            if want_unlabeled:
702	                if not (stored is None or stored == ""):
703	                    continue
704	                current = None
705	            else:
706	                if stored != label:
707	                    continue
708	                current = stored
709	            samples.append(
710	                {
711	                    "sha256": item["sha256"],
712	                    "source": item["source"],
713	                    "size": item["size"],
714	                    "label": current,
715	                }
716	            )
717	        samples.sort(key=lambda sample: sample["sha256"])
718	        return {"label": label, "count": len(samples), "samples": samples}

744	    def submit_batch(self, data: Any) -> dict[str, Any]:
745	        """Validate and apply a batch label update.
746	
747	        Parsing happens before the lock; inside the lock the submission
748	        runs through clearly separated stages, each with one job:
749	
750	        1. **Unknown samples** — every named digest must be registered; the
751	           first unknown one rejects the batch with nothing written.
752	        2. **Number identity** — a batch number already in history either
753	           replays the first submission's result (same content) or is a
754	           conflict (different content); neither touches the manifest.
755	        3. **Verification/classification** — each current label is read
756	           once: an expected-old mismatch rejects the batch, and the same
757	           reading decides whether that record actually changes.
758	        4. **Application** — only records classified as changed are
759	           mutated; if none are, the batch occupies no number and writes
760	           no history.
761	        5. **History and save** — the entry and result are assembled from
762	           the applied records, and manifest plus history commit together
763	           through the journal.
764	
765	        No stage mutates anything before every earlier stage has passed, so
766	        a rejection can neither leave partially updated samples nor a
767	        partial history entry.
768	        """
769	        number, records = parse_batch_file(data)
770	        with self._locked(create=True):
771	            manifest = self._read()
772	            history = self._read_history()
773	            items = {item["sha256"]: item for item in manifest["items"]}
774	
775	            # Stage 1: every record must name a registered sample.
776	            reject_unknown_samples(records, items.__contains__)
777	
778	            # Stage 2: a known number is replayed or conflicts; a fresh
779	            # number proceeds without examining the current labels.
780	            existing = next(
781	                (entry for entry in history["batches"] if entry["batch"] == number),
782	                None,
783	            )
784	            replay = resolve_re_submission(number, records, existing)
785	            if replay is not None:
786	                return replay
787	
788	            # Stage 3: verify expected old labels and classify changed vs
789	            # unchanged in a single current-label pass.
790	            resolutions = verify_records(
791	                records,
792	                lambda digest: normalize_label(items[digest].get("label")),
793	            )
794	
795	            # Stage 4: apply is the only mutation.  No changes at all
796	            # occupies no batch number and writes no history.
797	            if not any(resolution.changed for resolution in resolutions):
798	                return no_changes_result(number, len(records))
799	            applied_records = apply_resolutions(resolutions, items)
800	
801	            # Stage 5: assemble history, then save manifest and history
802	            # together through the journal.
803	            entry = build_history_entry(number, applied_records)
804	            history["batches"].append(entry)
805	            self._commit(manifest, history)
806	            return result_payload(number, "applied", applied_records)
807	
808	    def undo_batch(self, number: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
809	        """Undo a successful batch by number.
810	
811	        Only samples the batch actually changed are checked: each must have
812	        the same label revision it had right after the batch (no later
813	        modification, even one that restored the same label).  Repeated
814	        undos are idempotent and do not add history.
815	
816	        Integrity comes before either verdict: the target batch must list
817	        every sample exactly once, carry a sound pinned revision on each
818	        record, explicitly save both before/after labels on each record,
819	        and have every record's ``changed`` flag agree with the
820	        before/after labels saved on that same record.  A duplicated
821	        digest, a bad row, a missing label field or a flag that
822	        contradicts its labels rejects the undo even when the batch is
823	        already marked undone, so corruption is never hidden behind an
824	        ``already-undone`` success or confused with a sample modified
825	        after the batch.
826	        """
827	        with self._locked(create=True):
828	            manifest = self._read()
829	            history = self._read_history()
830	            entry = next(
831	                (entry for entry in history["batches"] if entry["batch"] == number),
832	                None,
833	            )
834	            if entry is None:
835	                raise BatchError(f"unknown batch number: {number!r}")
836	
837	            # Validate the target batch's integrity — one row per sample,
838	            # sound pinned revisions, both before/after labels saved, and
839	            # a changed flag that matches those labels — before the
840	            # already-undone short-circuit and the later-modification
841	            # checks: a duplicated, inconsistent or corrupt history record
842	            # is refusal, not an undo, a no-op or an unknown batch, and
843	            # nothing is rewritten.
844	            require_intact_history_records(entry)
845	            require_intact_history_revisions(entry)
846	            require_intact_history_labels(entry)
847	            require_intact_history_changes(entry)
848	
849	            if entry["undone"]:
850	                return {"batch": number, "status": "already-undone", "restored": 0}
851	
852	            items = {item["sha256"]: item for item in manifest["items"]}
853	            for record in entry["records"]:
854	                if not record["changed"]:
855	                    continue
856	                item = items.get(record["sha256"])
857	                if item is None:
858	                    raise BatchError(
859	                        f"cannot undo batch {number!r}: sample {record['sha256']} "
860	                        "is no longer in the manifest"
861	                    )
862	                current = normalize_label(item.get("label"))
863	                # record["rev"] is now known to be a genuine non-negative
864	                # integer, so a boolean/decimal/string can never compare
865	                # equal to the sample's current revision.  The stored
866	                # after-label is normalized before comparing: history may
867	                # explicitly save either unlabeled spelling (null or ""),
868	                # and both match a sample currently unlabeled either way.
869	                if item_revision(item) != record["rev"] or current != normalize_label(
870	                    record["new"]
871	                ):
872	                    raise BatchError(
873	                        f"cannot undo batch {number!r}: sample {record['sha256']} "
874	                        "was modified after the batch"
875	                    )
876	
877	            restored = 0
878	            for record in entry["records"]:
879	                if not record["changed"]:
880	                    continue
881	                item = items[record["sha256"]]
882	                item["label"] = record["old"]
883	                item["rev"] = item_revision(item) + 1
884	                restored += 1
885	
886	            entry["undone"] = True
887	            entry["undone_at"] = datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()
888	            self._commit(manifest, history)
889	            return {"batch": number, "status": "undone", "restored": restored}
890	
891	    def history(self) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
892	        """Return successful batch entries in submission order."""
893	        with self._locked():
894	            return self._read_history()["batches"]

900	    @contextmanager
901	    def _workspace_lock(self):
902	        """Exclusive workspace lock for check-and-write transactions.
903	
904	        ``flock`` is advisory but sufficient for local processes: holders
905	        serialize, so every read-modify-write observes the state left by the
906	        previous completed operation.
907	        """
908	        self.state_directory.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
909	        descriptor = os.open(self.lock_path, os.O_RDWR | os.O_CREAT, 0o600)
910	        try:
911	            fcntl.flock(descriptor, fcntl.LOCK_EX)
912	            yield
913	        finally:
914	            try:
915	                fcntl.flock(descriptor, fcntl.LOCK_UN)
916	            finally:
917	                os.close(descriptor)
918	
919	    @contextmanager
920	    def _locked(self, *, create: bool = False):
921	        """Hold the workspace lock and finish any leftover prepared journal.
922	
923	        Recovery runs once the lock is held, so a long-lived process that
924	        only imports, queries or creates plans still installs the prepared
925	        transaction of a process that crashed on this machine, without
926	        needing to reopen the workspace.
927	
928	        Read callers leave ``create`` false: on a workspace whose state
929	        directory does not yet exist there is no journal to finish and
930	        nothing for a writer to hold, so the query proceeds (and fails or
931	        reports empty exactly as before) without materializing one.
932	        """
933	        if not create and not self.state_directory.exists():
934	            yield
935	            return
936	        with self._workspace_lock():
937	            self._recover_transaction_locked()
938	            yield
939	
940	    def _recover_if_needed(self) -> None:
941	        """Finish a prepared transaction left by a crashed process."""
942	        if not self.transaction_path.exists():
943	            return
944	        with self._locked():
945	            pass
946	
947	    def _recover_transaction_locked(self) -> None:
948	        if not self.transaction_path.exists():
949	            return
950	        try:
951	            journal = json.loads(self.transaction_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
952	        except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError) as error:
953	            raise BatchError(f"cannot recover interrupted transaction: {error}") from error
954	        manifest = journal.get("manifest")
955	        history = journal.get("batches")
956	        if not isinstance(history, dict):
957	            raise BatchError("cannot recover interrupted transaction: journal is malformed")
958	        # Only install a coherent, fully valid pair, so recovery can never
959	        # replace the committed manifest with a structurally broken sample
960	        # list (a missing field, a bad field type or a duplicated digest):
961	        # the check runs before either file is rewritten, leaving both the
962	        # last committed registration and its history untouched.
963	        try:
964	            validate_manifest(manifest)
965	        except ManifestError as error:
966	            raise BatchError(
967	                f"cannot recover interrupted transaction: {error}"
968	            ) from error
969	        validate_history(history)
970	        # Idempotent installs: both files end up at the journal's version.
971	        self._write_json_atomic(self.manifest_path, manifest)
972	        self._write_json_atomic(self.batches_path, history)
973	        try:
974	            self.transaction_path.unlink()
975	        except OSError:
976	            pass
977	
978	    def _commit(self, manifest: dict[str, Any], history: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
979	        """Atomically install the new manifest and history together.
980	
981	        A write-ahead journal holding both full payloads is written and
982	        fsynced first; a crash at any point leaves enough to redo the
983	        missing install on the next open, so the two files never disagree.
984	        """
985	        journal = {"manifest": manifest, "batches": history}
986	        self._write_json_atomic(self.transaction_path, journal)
987	        self._write_json_atomic(self.manifest_path, manifest)
988	        self._write_json_atomic(self.batches_path, history)
989	        try:
990	            self.transaction_path.unlink()
991	        except OSError:
992	            pass
993	
994	    def _read_history(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
995	        if not self.batches_path.exists():
996	            return empty_history()
997	        try:
998	            data = json.loads(self.batches_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
999	        except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError) as error:
1000	            raise BatchError(f"cannot read batch history: {error}") from error
1001	        return validate_history(data)

1007	    def create_split(
1008	        self, name: str, seed: int, ratios: list[float | int | str | Fraction]
1009	    ) -> SplitPlanResult:
1010	        """Create (or reuse) a named train/validation/test plan.
1011	
1012	        The plan snapshots every sample currently in the manifest.  A
1013	        second call with the same name returns the stored plan unchanged
1014	        when the inputs match; otherwise it reports a name conflict.
1015	        """
1016	        validate_name(name)
1017	        if isinstance(seed, bool) or not isinstance(seed, int):
1018	            raise SplitError(f"Seed must be an integer, got {seed!r}")
1019	        fraction_ratios = validate_ratios(ratios)
1020	
1021	        self.initialize()
1022	        plan_path = self._split_path(name)
1023	
1024	        with self._locked(create=True):
1025	            # Sample identities and labels are read from one complete
1026	            # manifest state, so a batch committing concurrently is observed
1027	            # either entirely (all its label changes) or not at all.
1028	            items = self._read()["items"]
1029	            # assign() validates identities and performs the stratification.
1030	            assignment = assign(items, fraction_ratios, seed)
1031	
1032	            snapshot = [
1033	                {
1034	                    "sha256": item["sha256"],
1035	                    "label": item.get("label"),
1036	                    "source": item.get("source"),
1037	                }
1038	                for item in sorted(items, key=lambda item: item["sha256"])
1039	            ]
1040	            plan_payload = self._build_plan(
1041	                name, seed, fraction_ratios, snapshot, assignment
1042	            )
1043	
1044	            # The check-and-create is atomic under the same lock, so among
1045	            # concurrent creations of one name exactly one reports success;
1046	            # matching requests reuse it and differing ones conflict.
